items.title: Tom Porrello interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 6, 2023
items.q: My playing with Woody asked me to stay after the recording until they found somebody so I stayed for a couple, three weeks or something.

ctx.x: I’m glad you did that. A couple of more questions and then we’ll wrap up. If you got nostalgic, you felt nostalgic and you wanted to hear a particular LP and a particular tune that you really did shine on and you went and got the LPs out, what would that song be?

There’d be a couple of them. One of my favorites, again, is “The Toothless Grin” with Woody’s band. The story behind that, I was working at a hotel and I got called about — we played midnight until by the time I got home it was 2:30, and they said, “Can you get the first flight out tomorrow and fly down to San Francisco and finish this recording with us.” And I said — you know I had to call the band leader and get the okay and I went down and did it. So I had very little sleep and we went down there and they…

chart out and the band of course had played it on the road so they were well aware of it and they didn’t have to sight read it. But I had to sight read it. And I don’t know it was just swinging so good and everything, I just got into it and just let it fly you know. And there’s two tunes, the tune before that is a ballad too, “Come Rain or Come Shine.” Those are the two. “Come Rain or Come Shine” and “Toothless Grin” those are the last two that I did. Then there was another one I did but it’s on a different Woody…
